papers.title: Stability of solutions to stochastic partial differential equations
papers.abstract: We provide a general framework for the stability of solutions to stochastic partial differential equations with respect to perturbations of the drift. More precisely, we consider stochastic partial differential equations with drift given as the subdifferential of a convex function and prove continuous dependence of the solutions with regard to random Mosco convergence of the convex potentials. In particular, we identify the concept of stochastic variational inequalities (SVI) as a well-suited framework to study such stability properties. The generality of the developed framework is then laid out by deducing Trotter type and homogenization results for stochastic fast diffusion and stochastic singular p-Laplace equations. In addition, we provide an SVI treatment for stochastic nonlocal p-Laplace equations and prove their convergence to the respective local models.

papers.title: Talagrand Concentration Inequalities for Stochastic Partial Differential Equations
papers.abstract: One way to define the concentration of measure phenomenon is via Talagrand inequalities, also called transportation-information inequalities. That is, a comparison of the Wasserstein distance from the given measure to any other absolutely continuous measure with finite relative entropy. Such transportation-information inequalities were recently established for some stochastic differential equations. Here, we develop a similar theory for some stochastic partial differential equations.

summary: The literature on regularity and singularity propagation in stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) emphasizes the importance of stability and regularity properties under various noise conditions, particularly nonlinear multiplicative noise. Additionally, the application of Talagrand concentration inequalities to SPDEs marks a significant advancement in understanding concentration phenomena. However, gaps remain regarding the generalizability of findings across different types of SPDEs and the practical implications of these inequalities, highlighting the need for further research in these areas.
scholarly_positioning: Existing research on regularity and stability in stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) has primarily focused on specific types of noise and perturbations, revealing significant insights into solution properties. However, many studies are limited by their narrow scope, particularly in their applicability to more complex or higher-dimensional SPDEs. Additionally, the exploration of concentration inequalities, while promising, lacks comprehensive application across various stochastic contexts, leaving a gap in understanding their broader implications. This proposed research aims to address these unresolved tensions by expanding the analysis of regularity and singularity propagation in SPDEs, thereby contributing to a more robust theoretical framework that can accommodate diverse stochastic influences and enhance practical applications.
research_scope: This study will focus on the regularity and stability of solutions to stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) with a specific emphasis on nonlinear multiplicative noise. The target model will involve higher-dimensional SPDEs to assess the robustness of solutions under various stochastic influences. The evaluation period will encompass a comprehensive analysis of solution properties over time, utilizing theoretical frameworks and regularity analysis techniques. The primary outcomes will include the identification of regularity properties and stability metrics of the solutions, while secondary outcomes will explore the implications of concentration inequalities on the behavior of these solutions. A control group will consist of solutions to simpler, well-studied SPDEs for comparative analysis.

The mediator is the regularity and stability of the solutions, which are influenced by the nature of the nonlinear multiplicative noise. The moderator is the dimensionality of the SPDEs, affecting how different perturbations manifest in solution properties. proposal: This research proposal aims to investigate the regularity and stability of solutions to higher-dimensional stochastic partial differential equations (SPDEs) with nonlinear multiplicative noise, addressing the critical gap in the literature regarding the influence of diverse stochastic perturbations on solution properties. Key concepts include SPDEs, defined as equations incorporating randomness in their formulation; regularity, representing the smoothness of solutions; stability, indicating the boundedness of solutions under perturbations; and concentration inequalities, which provide bounds on the probability of deviations in random variables. The study is technically feasible as it relies on theoretical analysis rather than empirical data, utilizing existing frameworks and regularity analysis techniques. Background literature highlights significant insights into specific noise types but lacks generalizability across various stochastic influences, particularly in higher-dimensional contexts. The central research question is: How do varying types of stochastic perturbations influence the regularity and stability of solutions to higher-dimensional SPDEs compared to simpler, well-studied SPDEs? The theoretical mechanism posits that the type of stochastic perturbation (independent variable) affects the regularity and stability of solutions (mediators), which in turn impacts the robustness of solutions (dependent variable), moderated by the dimensionality of the SPDEs. The hypothesis is that higher-dimensional SPDEs subjected to varying perturbations will exhibit significantly different regularity and stability properties compared to simpler SPDEs, with increased complexity in perturbations leading to decreased regularity and stability. Constructs will be operationalized through metrics such as Sobolev norms for regularity and Lyapunov exponents for stability, with a control group of simpler SPDEs for comparative analysis. The methodology involves categorizing perturbations, applying regularity analysis techniques, and ensuring validity through rigorous theoretical analysis. Expected contributions include a comprehensive theoretical framework elucidating the interplay between stochastic influences and solution properties, novel regularity analysis techniques tailored for higher-dimensional SPDEs, and a foundation for future empirical investigations. Key limitations include potential misclassification of perturbations and the inability to generalize findings beyond the studied SPDEs, as well as the risk of numerical approximation errors and uncontrolled external factors affecting solution behavior.
